description: pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:195-200 — NoValidPath carries the inner pkix_path::Error as String (via {e} formatting), justified in the rustdoc by "so Error retains its Hash derive (the upstream error enum does not implement Hash)". This is a deliberate tradeoff but locks consumers out of: programmatic match on inner error variants (e.g. detecting SignatureInvalid vs NameConstraintViolation vs TimeNotValid distinctly), serde round-trip preserving the inner variant structure (the String is opaque), and any future caller that wants to retry on specific failure modes. The escape hatch "drop down to build_path_candidates and call validate_path per candidate themselves" forces every such consumer to reimplement the iterate-and-validate loop. Two paths forward: (a) make Hash derive on Error optional or drop it (Hash is unused elsewhere in the workspace — verify), or (b) add a typed last_error field gated by a feature or a separate variant. The Hash derive on Error has no test or doc justification — search the workspace and confirm whether dropping Hash is acceptable. If it is, NoValidPath { tried, last_error: Box<pkix_path::Error> } is the principled shape. `pkix-chain` already box-wraps a pkix_path_builder::Error so the change does not cascade. Bears on AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly serde-round-trippable result types): right now the inner error is unreviewable after serde round-trip.
title: Error::NoValidPath { last_error: String } locks consumers out of programmatic match on inner pkix_path::Error
